jobs.description:
**Assistant Professor, Mathematics (Tenure- Track)**

  
  
**Posting Number:** F01362  
**Location:** Los Medanos College  
**Salary:**
  
  
**Description of Position:**  
Los Medanos College's Math Department has 11 full-time faculty members and is excited for a new member. With the advent of AB705/1705 the number of students enrolling in first-level transfer courses has increased. The Math department seeks faculty who are familiar with instructional techniques, institutional resources, and can direct students to the appropriate resources to support the diverse first-level transfer students. Recently, the LMC Math department has been remodeling the coursework pathways and designing new courses such as Quantitative Reasoning and even Calculus Support. This position can teach a wide variety of courses in the Math department, including transfer-level coursework and major/STEM level coursework. Other department duties will involve working with teams in meeting their goals of strategically remodeling and design to increase the quality of teaching and learning and equitable outcomes for all students taking math at LMC. Our department is committed to increasing the success and retention rates in math classes for Black students at LMC. We are also improving our curriculum to be more culturally responsive. We are looking for instructors who share a strong commitment to pedagogies that close equity gaps.  
  
**Inquiries:**  
Email Nicole Acosta at nacosta@losmedanos.edu if you have a question.  
  
**Position Status:** Tenure- Track  
**EEO Job Category:** Faculty & Other Instructional Staff  
**Employee Group:** Full-Time Faculty  
**Department:** L5009-Mathematics  
  
**Duties and Responsibilities:**  
In addition to contractual duties, all full-time faculty are expected to participate actively in their disciplines, department activities, and the general intellectual life and governance of the college. Part of the teaching assignment may be in the evening and/or online. Duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:  
1. advancing equitable student learning through dedicated, exemplary instruction in accordance with established course outlines;  
2. participating in the assessment of student learning outcomes for courses and programs; developing and implementing student learning outcomes assessment processes for courses and programs;  
3. collaborating in the development and revision of curriculum and in program review;  
4. engaging in department program improvement initiatives;  
5. participating in department, division, and college committees;  
6. participating in professional development activities, both departmental and college-wide;  
7. maintaining current knowledge in the subject matter area and effective teaching/ learning strategies;  
8. maintaining appropriate standards of professional conduct and ethics;  
9. informing students of course requirements, evaluation procedures and attendance requirements;  
10. preparing and grading class assignments and examinations and informing students of their academic progress;  
11. maintaining attendance, scholastic, and personnel records and submitting them according to published deadlines;  
12. posting and holding sufficient and regular office hours in accordance with prevailing policy;  
13. participating in College's shared governance processes.  
  
**Minimum Qualification-Education/Experience:**  
Master's in mathematics or applied mathematics OR Bachelor's in either of the above AND Master's in statistics, physics or mathematics education OR the equivalent. If you do not possess the listed degree, you can apply for an equivalency. You can upload a master's degree equivalency form in the attachment section of the application to explain how you possess the equivalent background.  
  
Understanding of and sensitivity to the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, sexual orientation and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, staff and faculty.  
  
**Desirable Qualifications:**  
#1: Ability and willingness to support students in various mathematics courses including courses with support, i.e., Statistics with support, Precalculus with Support, and Applied Calculus with support, Calculus, Differential Equations, Linear Algebra, and/or Discrete Mathematics. Furthermore, willingness to provide adequate support to students in order to promote success and retention.  
  
#2: Ability to facilitate effective mathematical learning in the classroom of various teaching modalities (online synchronous, online asynchronous, face-to-face, or hybrid). Several strategies may include experience in utilizing innovative class discussions, facilitating student collaboration /group work, tutoring, discovery learning, and designing lab activities/ just-in-time support.
  
#3: Ability and willingness to integrate new and existing technology and Software/ Tools into the curriculum. These include Desmos or any calculator suite, Statcrunch, R, Geogebra, OER, etc.  
  
#4: Demonstrate experience and/or willingness to participate as a team member or leader in committees. Some examples are as follows: Math Path To Transfer, Math Teaching Communities, and Various Math Cohorts (Puente, UMOJA, Honors, etc.).  
  
#5: Have sensitivity and understanding of diverse academic socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, including those with physical or learning disabilities.  
  
**Job Open Date:** 10/06/2026  
**Job Close Date:** 11/13/2026  
**Open Until Filled:** No  
**Employment Begins:** Fall 2027  
**# of Months:** 12

jobs.title: Faculty, Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL)
jobs.description:
**Description**
**About Arkansas Colleges of Health Education**
Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE) is a private, non-profit, graduate-level health sciences institution located on over 500 acres in Fort Smith, Arkansas. ACHE’s service-driven mission is to educate and train a diverse group of competent and compassionate healthcare professionals; to create health and research support facilities; and to provide healthy living environments to improve the lives of others. Founded in 2014, ACHE has experienced rapid growth and is poised to be a leader in healthcare education for years to come. ACHE is the first and only private institution in Arkansas that is dedicated solely to healthcare and wellness, and maintains a strong commitment to the surrounding community.
  
  
**About Fort Smith And The Arkansas River Valley**
Fort Smith is a vibrant community of around 90,000, with a low cost of living and ample recreational opportunities. Located in the beautiful Arkansas River Valley at the foothills of the Ozark mountains, Fort Smith is nestled between the Ozark-St. Francis and Ouachita National Forests. The region provides hiking, mountain biking, rock climbing, hang gliding, whitewater rafting, and camping all within a short drive. In addition, the city supports a variety of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, an award-winning symphony, and two historic entertainment districts.
  
  
**LOCATION**
This is a hybrid position. The employee will be remote the majority of the time, with the supervisor determining any residential requirements.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL) Faculty member is a collaborative educator and scholar committed to excellence in graduate education, executive leadership development, scholarship, service, and continuous program improvement.
  
  
The faculty member will contribute to the delivery and ongoing development of the Doctor of Executive Leadership program through high-quality online instruction, curriculum development, student advising and mentorship, scholarly activity, program assessment, and institutional and professional service.
  
  
The faculty member will work collaboratively with the DEL Program Director, faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership to support the mission, vision, goals, and continued growth of the DEL program and Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE).
  
  
The faculty member will carry a teaching load as assigned based on program needs and institutional expectations and will actively contribute to the academic, scholarly, and service missions of ACHE.
  
  
**Essential Functions And Responsibilities**
**Teaching and Curriculum**

* Teach online Doctor of Executive Leadership courses within areas of demonstrated academic or professional competence.
* Provide high-quality, engaging, doctoral-level instruction appropriate for experienced working professionals and executive leaders.
* Develop, review, and revise course content, instructional materials, learning activities, and assessments.
* Ensure alignment among course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, instructional activities, and assessments.
* Maintain current, evidence-informed course content reflecting contemporary leadership theory, organizational practice, healthcare, business, policy, and other relevant areas.
* Utilize effective online teaching methodologies and educational technologies to promote student engagement and learning.
* Provide timely, substantive, and constructive feedback on student assignments and academic performance.
* Maintain consistent course organization, communication, grading practices, and academic expectations.
* Participate in continuous curriculum review and improvement.
* Support the development of new DEL courses, concentrations, certificates, educational pathways, and other curricular initiatives as assigned.
* Maintain the security and integrity of course materials, assessments, student information, and academic records.
* Teach courses in other ACHE programs when appropriate based on expertise and institutional needs.

**Student Advising and Mentorship**

* Serve as an academic advisor and mentor to DEL students as assigned.
* Maintain appropriate availability and responsiveness to students.
* Monitor student academic progression and provide guidance when academic or professional development needs are identified.
* Provide individualized mentorship that connects doctoral education with students' professional leadership goals and organizational impact.
* Support students experiencing academic difficulty and participate in remediation activities when appropriate.
* Refer student concerns involving academic performance, professionalism, or conduct to the DEL Program Director in accordance with institutional policies.
* Support student scholarly activities, presentations, publications, professional development, and other academic opportunities.
* Promote a supportive, inclusive, professional, and academically rigorous learning environment.

**Scholarship and Research**

* Maintain an active program of scholarship appropriate to academic rank, professional expertise, and institutional expectations.
* Engage in research, applied scholarship, scholarly writing, peer-reviewed publication, professional presentations, or other recognized forms of scholarly activity.
* Pursue opportunities for collaborative scholarship with DEL faculty, ACHE faculty, students, and external partners.
* Mentor DEL students in scholarly inquiry, evidence-based leadership, research, and dissemination of scholarly work when appropriate.
* Participate in the development and evaluation of DEL program-related research and scholarly initiatives.
* Seek opportunities to translate research and professional experience into knowledge that advances executive leadership, organizational performance, healthcare, education, or other relevant fields.
* Pursue external funding, grants, or collaborative research opportunities when appropriate.
* Disseminate scholarly work at local, state, national, and international professional forums.

**Program Assessment and Continuous Improvement**

* Participate in the ongoing assessment and evaluation of the DEL curriculum and program.
* Assist with evaluation of course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, student performance, and other measures of program effectiveness.
* Participate in the collection, analysis, and interpretation of assessment data.
* Contribute to accreditation, institutional effectiveness, and continuous quality-improvement activities as assigned.
* Participate in periodic review and revision of course materials, curriculum, academic policies, and program processes.
* Provide recommendations to the DEL Program Director regarding opportunities to improve academic quality, student outcomes, and program effectiveness.
* Maintain required academic and administrative documentation in accordance with ACHE policies and applicable accreditation standards

**Program and Institutional Service**

* Serve as a member of DEL program committees and other ACHE committees as assigned.
* Participate in faculty meetings, curriculum meetings, assessment activities, retreats, and other institutional responsibilities.
* Participate in DEL admissions activities, including applicant review, interviews, and candidate evaluation as requested.
* Support DEL orientation, information sessions, recruitment events, student activities, and other program initiatives.
* Participate in faculty governance and institutional service activities consistent with academic appointment and institutional expectations.
* Collaborate with faculty and staff across ACHE programs to advance interdisciplinary education and institutional initiatives.
* Support the mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities of ACHE.
* Participate in commencement, academic ceremonies, institutional events, and other activities requiring faculty representation as appropriate.

**Recruitment and Program Growth**

* Support recruitment and enrollment initiatives for the DEL program.
* Participate in information sessions, webinars, conferences, professional meetings, and other recruitment activities as requested.
* Engage professional networks and organizations to increase awareness of the DEL program.
* Identify opportunities for educational partnerships, professional collaborations, and student recruitment.
* Support development of relationships with healthcare systems, academic institutions, professional organizations, government agencies, military organizations, nonprofit organizations, and other potential partners when appropriate.
* Assist in identifying emerging leadership-development needs and opportunities that may inform future DEL curriculum and program growth.

**Professional and External Engagement**

* Maintain active engagement within relevant professional and academic communities.
* Represent ACHE and the DEL program professionally at conferences, meetings, educational events, and community activities.
* Participate in local, state, regional, national, or international professional service appropriate to expertise and academic role.
* Develop relationships that may contribute to educational opportunities, research, scholarship, student development, or institutional partnerships.
* Maintain professional competence and remain current within areas of academic and professional expertise.

**Faculty Responsibilities And Professional Conduct**

* Maintain professional, ethical, and collegial relationships with students, faculty, staff, institutional leadership, and external partners.

jobs.title: Adjunct Professor - CSPP: Clinical PsyD Program- San Diego Campus Candidate Pool
jobs.description:
The Clinical PSYD Program in San Diego follows a Practitioner-Scholar model that emphasizes the applications of theory and research to clinical practice. The program develops competent professional health-care psychologists skilled in delivering a variety of clinical services to diverse populations in varied settings. The program’s most distinctive component is its dual emphasis on clinical expertise and clinical scholarship. Students take courses in a wide range of subjects, including statistics, theories of personality, psychological assessment, multicultural issues, and psychological practice. Students may follow their own clinical interests and further their individual career goals by selecting a specialized series of courses, research, and field placements related to a particular area of practice.

**Application Description:**

Applicants to this position will be considered for a candidate pool encompassing one or more of the subject areas outlined in the job description. This pool will be used to identify qualified candidates for potential appointments during the 2026–2027 academic year.

**Salary Range:**
$39 - $46 hourly (based on course requirements & level of education). This is a temporary, non-benefits eligible role.

Qualifications

**Minimum Requirements:**

* **Education:**
  Doctoral or other terminal degree in Psychology or associated field, from an accredited college or university.
* **Experience:**
  Appropriate experience in the areas(s) of specialization and expertise
* **Certifications, Licenses, etc.:**
  Clinical Psychology license required for clinical courses.

Additional Information

**Specific Courses:**

**Fall 2026 (Aug. 17, 2026 – Dec. 20, 2026)**

**PSY60300 Advanced Statistics**

The objective of this 3-unit course is to understand applied research methodology, evaluate and synthesize psychological research literature, and apply both to clinical challenges. The course will provide an overview of the major statistical tools employed in contemporary behavioral science research and program evaluation. Topics surveyed will be the philosophy of science and scientific method; descriptive and inferential statistics; univariate and multivariate analysis of variance and co-variance (one-way and factorial); regression techniques; principal and (exploratory and confirmatory) factor analysis; power calculation and corrections for multiple comparisons.

**Spring 2027 (Jan 4, 2027 – May 16, 2027)**

**PSY61122 Social Basis of Behavior**

This 2-unit course will enable students to develop competence and understanding of clinical implications with respect to:

* The social development of the self (e.g., self-perception and self-efficacy).
* Interpersonal relations (e.g., attraction, love, and marriage).
* Attitude formation and change; aggression.
* Social influences (e.g., conformity, obedience).
* Attribution and social cognition.
* Group behavior and performance.
* Culture, prejudice and stigma.



**PSY65400 Family Systems Theory**

This 2-unit course will prepare students to be effective professional therapists who have increased awareness in the following areas:

* Overviews of the theories of family therapy and evidence based principles.
* Practical applications of Family Systems Theory.
* Connection between Family Systems Theory and clinical practice.
* Social, cultural, political and economic issues and contexts in Family Therapy.
* Develop knowledge of the assessment, diagnosis, and treatment planning as related to Family Systems Theory.

**PSY61050 Biological Aspects of Behavior**

This 3-unit course is designed to provide the graduate student in psychology with a comprehensive overview of the field of biological psychology. The purpose of the course is for students:

* To develop an understanding of the research results, research methodology, and techniques of data collection/analysis in the area of biological psychology.
* To demonstrate intermediate knowledge the core areas of biological psychology.
* To display critical scientific thinking in the area of biological psychology.
* To develop the ability to review, evaluate, and synthesize biological psychology research.
* To utilize this theoretical and scientific knowledge as a basis for the effective practice of clinical psychology.

**PSY61402 Developmental Psychology**

This two-unit course for second year Psy.D. students covers a wide range of developmental stages and topics including both adaptive and challenging developmental pathways. The course includes a study of developmental theories, psychopathology, constructs, research and research methods as they contribute to an understanding of normal human development and its variants. Psychological development from conception through aging and death are covered. Contemporary issues and trends are discussed. All areas of development covered in this course will be studied and considered within appropriate cultural contexts.

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

* Compare and contrast numerous theories of physical, cognitive and social/emotional development.
* Apply research and theories of development across the lifespan within a broad social and cultural context.
* Acquire knowledge to think critically about varying development trajectories when determining adaptive and maladaptive
* developmental pathways.
* More fully understand how their life experiences and own development influence their understanding of human development.



**PSY65030 Personality Assessment I**

The purpose of this 3 unit course is to subject students to a wide variety of the most widely utilized personality instruments in psychology today and to learn how to generate a psychological report that is accurate, supportive and has the potential to change the patient’s trajectory. Following the course on Intellectual Assessment students completing PSY 6503- Personality Assessment I will be subjected to, and demonstrate mastery of the following personality assessment components:

**History of personality assessment.**

The development of various significant personality assessment instruments.

Proper test selection for adults and children as well as referral question.

How to write a detailed, accurate, and compassionate psychological report.

How to develop a diagnosis with the aid of personality test data.

How to develop meaningful recommendations from personality test data.

**PSY60140 Qualitative Methods of Research**

The purpose of this 3-unit course is to subject students to a wide variety of the most widely utilized personality instruments in psychology today and to learn how to generate a psychological report that is accurate, supportive and has the potential to change the patient’s trajectory. Following the course on Intellectual Assessment students completing PSY 6503- Personality Assessment I will be subjected to, and demonstrate mastery of the following personality assessment components:

**History of personality assessment**

The development of various significant personality assessment instruments

Proper test selection for adults and children as well as referral question

How to write a detailed, accurate, and compassionate psychological report

How to develop a diagnosis with the aid of personality test data

How to develop meaningful recommendations from personality test data

**PSY60310 Statistics, Psychometrics, and Research Design**

This 3-unit course is designed to prepare students to achieve graduate-level knowledge in the discipline-specific knowledge areas of Research Methods, Statistical Analysis, and Psychometrics and the profession-wide competency of Research. The goal of this course is an understanding of the principles and methods of psychological research, which will include areas of hypothesis testing, experimental design options, sample selection, control group strategies, criteria and criterion measures, psychometrics, data analysis, and interpretation of results. The course will enable students to understand how research is properly done and to discriminate between adequate and inadequate research conclusions. The pros and cons of experimental versus nonexperimental research will be examined, and those of quantitative versus qualitative research, among other issues. This training should prepare students to become enlightened consumers as well as potential producers of research and for the application of research methods to program evaluation

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

* Facilitating Classroom and Distance/Distributed Learning.
* Course and syllabus preparation.

* Mentoring and advising students.

**Skills:**

* The ability to work independently and be self-motivated.
* High level of accuracy and attention to detail and the ability to problem solve.
* The ability to explain complex requirements in clear and concise terms.
* The ability to be flexible with workflow to meet the needs of the department and students and to manage multiple tasks per required deadlines.
* The drive to encourage, direct, hold accountable and guide candidates toward task completion.
* Must demonstrate the ability to work as an effective team member and develop trusting relationships with students and Alliant employees, as well as the Registrar’s Office and various academic departments.
* Culturally humble and ability to communicate and interact effectively with diverse people.
* Highly motivated, focused and results oriented.
* Ability to exercise discretion and tact in all interpersonal interactions, and to maintain confidentiality.
* Collaboration and partnering with other university stakeholders to support candidate success.

The Department of Anesthesiology at SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University is seeking a full-time Professor & Chair. Reporting to the Dean of the College of Medicine, the successful candidate will:

+ A 4-year accredited Residency Program with 17 Residents at each training level

* Be responsible for administrative operations of the academic Department of Anesthesiology in the College of Medicine.
* Be responsible for the oversight and success of the academic mission of the department and its faculty throughout the DHSU academic system, including its teaching enterprise in medical student education (UME), resident education (GME), and Continuing Medical Education (CME), as well as the department's research enterprise.
* Work with leadership of University Hospital at Downstate and its affiliated teaching hospitals (which include Kings County Hospital Center, Maimonides Medical Center, the Brooklyn Veteran's Administration Medical Center, and One Brooklyn Health) and with the Clinical Practice Management Plan (Downstate Health Physicians), the Chair will be responsible for oversight of the academic programs and the associated clinical enterprise.
* Endeavor to advance faculty development in clinical and academic skills within the department and throughout the entire network.
* Act in concert with the Chair of the Department of Surgery in providing oversight of the Operating Rooms, and in working to improve the efficiency of Perioperative Services.
* Lead the faculty (both current and those recruited) at all sites in the development of innovative clinical and basic research initiatives, either independently or in collaboration with other investigators on our faculty, other schools, and community organizations. A reputation for path-breaking research will, in turn, enhance our ability to attract patients, referrals, and residents, creating the foundation for a new phase of departmental growth. It is expected that the faculty the Chair will recruit will significantly expand the range of services available to its patients while providing a superb educational experience for our residents and students.
* Maintain and enhance Downstate's residency program and our clerkship offering for medical students. Our graduates have long been recognized as being well prepared to make significant contributions in their discipline, but we believe that we can further enhance the quality and reputation of these programs and will rely on the Chair and the faculty to devote considerable attention to this task. Together with Downstate's academic partners, these programs will prepare the next generation of leaders and practitioners in this field for careers in Brooklyn, New York City, and the nation, and carve a place for Downstate as a leading center for state­ of-the-art anesthesiology services.
* Have the demonstrated capacity to foster an environment in which excellence in teaching, research and scholarship flourish, as well as experience in developing and leading clinical, educational and research programs. Candidates must have a record of effective administrative and fiscal leadership, national stature in academic Anesthesiology, demonstrated experience promoting a diverse workforce, excellent interpersonal skills, and positive interactions with faculty, students, and staff.

Department of Physics - UC Berkeley
  
  
The Physics Department at the University of California, Berkeley is actively recruiting for multiple tenure track Assistant Professor positions. These searches are in the following areas:
  
​
  

* Atomic, Molecular, & Optical (AMO) Physics Theory: We welcome applicants from across the full range of theoretical AMO subfields, especially those who will make fundamental contributions to theory and exhibit strong synergy with experimental AMO research. Candidates from subfields in quantum simulation, many-body quantum mechanics, emergent phenomena and entangled systems, connections to quantum information science, quantum optics, precision measurement and tests of fundamental physics, ultracold molecules and chemistry, ultrafast optics, and others are encouraged to apply.
* Condensed Matter Experiment: We welcome applicants across all areas, including but not limited to, quantum magnetism, topological phases, unconventional superconductivity, spintronics, and novel quantum order arising in exotic materials in three dimensional and low dimensional systems, such as van der Waals and layered heterostructures. Areas of expertise of interest include, but are not limited to, the synthesis of bulk and thin film materials, advanced spectroscopic and scattering techniques, quantum and mesoscopic transport, and microscopic imaging and scanning probe techniques. We also encourage applications at the interface of condensed matter physics and quantum information science.
* Open Search: We welcome applicants in a broad open search in space sciences, astrophysics, and experimental nuclear and particle physics. Areas of emphasis include space sciences, theory or experiment, including space and solar plasma physics, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, gamma ray astrophysics, multi-messenger astronomy, radio cosmology, cosmic rays, and dark matter; astrophysics experiment, including gravity wave detection and space plasma physics; observational and theoretical astrophysics focused on the use and development of data science techniques and machine learning; and experimental nuclear and particle physics focused on fundamental symmetries of nature, including CP and time reversal symmetry, family and lepton number symmetries, and matter-antimatter symmetry.

Applicants must submit a separate application to each position of interest.
  
  
Berkeley Physics and its partners are committed to establishing cultures that nurture scientific identity and remove barriers to entry, in order to strengthen pathways into careers. To that end, we strive to work and learn together in a positive and inclusive environment. Please visit UC Berkeley Physics' Equity & Inclusion website for more information.

Although all applicants for faculty recruitment must complete the entire application, applicants will only be subject to reference checks if and when they are selected as the candidate to whom the hiring unit would like to extend a formal offer. More information is available on this website .
  
  
**Qualifications :** PhD (or equivalent international degree) or enrolled in PhD or equivalent international degree-granting program at the time of application.

**Faculty Position – Osteopathic Principles & Practices / NMM/OMM**
The Meritus School of Osteopathic Medicine (MSOM), located on the campus of Meritus Health in Hagerstown, Maryland, is actively expanding its faculty. As the first new medical school in Maryland in more than a century, MSOM is committed to advancing osteopathic medical education, strengthening the physician workforce, and improving the health of the region through excellence in teaching, scholarship, and service.

Adjacent on‑campus housing at Meritus Commons provides residential accommodations for medical students and contributes to a vibrant academic community.

**faculty appointment in Osteopathic Principles & Practices (OPP) / Neuromusculoskeletal Medicine (NMM/OMM)**
. This faculty member contributes to the development, delivery, and continuous improvement of the OMM curriculum across the four‑year osteopathic medical program.

* Engages in scholarly activity, including research, presentations, and contributions to the academic community
* Supports departmental initiatives and contributes to the academic mission of the school

**Education**

* Demonstrated history of academic teaching and assessment in medical education

**About Us**
Oral Roberts University is a non-profit organization whose staff and faculty actually make a difference in the lives of its students. We pride ourselves on our culture and the values we uphold. Our team is passionate about what we do, and we want you to make us even better!
  
  
**Job Description**

* Full Time

Oral Roberts University - Anna Vaughn College of Nursing invites highly qualified applicants for this full-time position for Summer / Fall of 2023. The selected candidate will serve as a member of a course-specific teaching team and report directly to the Course Coordinator.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
The faculty member is expected to participate in the full range of faculty activities including, but not limited to, the following:
  
  

* Assuring that the nursing curriculum is consistent with the mission, philosophy, and goals of the School of Nursing and Oral Roberts University
* Implementing a concept-based curriculum
* Revising courses consistent with professional nursing practice and educational standards
* Selecting learning resources that maximize students' learning
* Implementing clinical experiences consistent with students' achievement of course objectives
* Providing leadership in the spiritual and professional growth of students
* Teaching in on-campus classes, simulated laboratories, and clinical settings
* Serving as an academic advisor to nursing students
* Serving on School of Nursing committees
* Serving on University Committees

**REQUIREMENTS**

* Master of Science in Nursing (minimum)
* Doctor of Nursing Practice or Ph.D., preferred
* Experience in community health, mental health, medical-surgical, pediatric, or critical care nursing
* If first teaching appointment, minimum 2 years clinical practice prior to appointment
* Meet qualifications for RN licensure in the state of Oklahoma
* Practice certifications appropriate to clinical practice area
* Lifestyle consistent with Oral Roberts University Honor Code - University faculty members are required to sign the University Honor Code and are expected to exemplify a lifestyle consistent with the standards for honor code living.

Application Deadline: Open until filled
  
  
**INSTRUCTIONS**

* Complete the ORU faculty application
* Please provide transcripts from all colleges and universities listed on your C.V. and application
* Please provide names and e-mail addresses for three references

**Equal Employment Opportunity**
*Oral Roberts University promotes equal employment opportunities for all individuals regardless of differences in race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.*

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor in Sport and Recreation Management
jobs.description:
**About FIU**

Florida International University is a Top 50, preeminent public research university with 55,000 students from all 50 states and more than 140 countries, as well as an alumni network of more than 340,000. Located in the global city of Miami, the university offers more than 200 degree programs at the undergraduate, graduate and professional levels, including medicine and law. FIU faculty are leaders in their fields and include National Academy members, Fulbright Scholars and MacArthur Genius Fellows. A Carnegie R1 institution, FIU drives impactful research in environmental resilience, health and technology and innovation. Home to the Wall of Wind and Institute of Environment, FIU stands at the forefront of discovery and innovation. With a focus on student success, economic mobility and community engagement, FIU is redefining what it means to be a public research university.

  
**Job Information**

**Assistant Teaching Professor in Sport and Recreation Management**

Position Description

The Department of Counseling, Recreation and School Psychology (CRSP) at Florida International University (FIU) invites applications for a full-time, 12-month, non-tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Teaching Professor in Sport and Recreation Management, to commence in the Fall semester of 2027.

Responsibilities

The appointed faculty member will have an assignment in the areas of instruction (90%) and service (10%).

The instruction assignment during the first year will be a 4/4/3 teaching load (11 courses in the academic year) and involve the delivery of undergraduate and/or graduate courses for the Sport and Recreation Management program, in in-person and online modalities. The appointee will also be expected to participate in student mentorship activities.

Beyond instruction, the position encompasses service contributions to support the department's mission. These may include assisting with the accreditation process of the sport management program, actively participating in curriculum meetings, and representing the department's standards and goals. Additionally, the successful candidate will be expected to maintain active involvement with industry and relevant professional associations to enhance our students' educational experiences and raise the profile of the program in the professional community.

Minimum Qualifications

* Terminal degree in Sports Management or a closely related field.
* Demonstrated effectiveness in instruction in a variety of modalities, including in-person and fully online courses at an institution of higher education.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Evidence of excellence in teaching, industry and leadership experience
* Strong organizational and communication skills.
* Ten (10) or more years of industry experience in a leadership role in Sport and Recreation Management

Salary

Nationally competitive and commensurate with experience based on appropriate salary survey.

About the Program

The Sport and Recreation Management Program is a vibrant and growing program with a healthy number of applicants and strong enrollment. It is situated within the Department of Counseling, Recreation, and School Psychology in the School of Education and Human Development at the College of Arts, Sciences, & Education (CASE). For undergraduate information, please visit: BS in Sport and Recreation Management, and for graduate information, visit: MS Sport and Recreation Management. We encourage individuals with the ability to enhance our department's interdisciplinary strengths, integrate sport and recreation, and foster collaborative partnerships across campus disciplines to apply.

Qualified candidates are encouraged to apply to Job Opening ID **538255**at careers.fiu.edu and attach a cover letter, a CV, a teaching philosophy statement, evidence of teaching effectiveness, and transcripts. Candidates will be requested to provide names and contact information for at least three (3) references who will be contacted as determined by the search committee. To receive full consideration, applications and required materials should be received by *November 1, 2026*. The review will continue until the position is filled. Please direct any questions to Hyejin Bang at bangh@fiu.edu.

  
**Job Category**

Faculty

jobs.description:
**Job Description & Requirements**
Family Medicine Residency Core Faculty
  
StartDate: ASAP Pay Rate: $250000.00 - $285000.00
  
  

Texas A&M / University Health seeks exceptional Family Medicine physicians to serve as Core Faculty in a transformative expansion that will establish a new academic and clinical presence in San Antonio through its strategic partnership with University Health.

This is a rare opportunity to join one of the nation's leading health sciences institutions at a pivotal moment of growth. As a founding faculty member, you will help shape the future of medical education in South Texas by teaching Texas A&M medical students, developing innovative clinical learning experiences, and laying the foundation for a future Family Medicine residency program.

Physicians joining this initiative will enjoy the unique combination of academic leadership, clinical practice, and program development while collaborating with respected leaders from Texas A&M Health and University Health. Your contributions will help create a lasting legacy for generations of learners and patients.

**Opportunity Highlights**

* Join Texas A&M Health during an exciting period of expansion into the San Antonio market
* Academic appointment at the Clinical Assistant Professor, Clinical Associate Professor, or Clinical Professor level, commensurate with experience
* Full-time academic professional-track position with an anticipated Fall 2027 start
* Opportunity to play a foundational role in developing a future Family Medicine residency program
* Teach and mentor medical students in both clinical and classroom settings
* Help design and implement innovative educational experiences for Texas A&M learners
* Maintain an active outpatient Family Medicine practice while pursuing academic interests
* Collaborate across one of Texas' largest and most respected academic-health system partnerships
* Competitive compensation and comprehensive Texas state employee benefits package

**Why Texas A&M Health & University Health?**

This landmark collaboration brings together the academic excellence of Texas A&M Health and the clinical strength of University Health, one of South Texas' premier health systems. Together, the organizations are creating a robust educational and clinical environment designed to expand physician training, improve access to care, and meet the growing healthcare needs of the region.

For physicians who value innovation, collaboration, and academic impact, this opportunity offers the chance to build something meaningful from the ground up.

Live and Thrive in San Antonio, Texas

San Antonio is one of the nation's fastest-growing metropolitan areas and offers an exceptional quality of life. The city blends rich history and culture with modern amenities, top-rated schools, a vibrant culinary scene, and a cost of living that remains more affordable than many major U.S. markets.

**Community Highlights**

* Exceptional livability with a strong sense of community and family-friendly neighborhoods
* Home to the iconic River Walk, the Alamo, and five UNESCO World Heritage-designated San Antonio Missions
* Thriving economy supported by healthcare, education, technology, military, and bioscience industries
* Year-round outdoor recreation, professional sports, and cultural attractions
* No state income tax and a lower cost of living than many comparable metropolitan areas
* Convenient access to Austin, the Texas Hill Country, and Gulf Coast destinations

**Job Benefits**
**About the Company**
At AMN Healthcare, we strive to be recognized as the most trusted, innovative, and influential force in helping healthcare organizations provide quality patient care that continually evolves to make healthcare more human, more effective, and more achievable.

### **Working/Functional Title**

Assistant Professor Tenure System

### **Position Summary**

Michigan State University's Eli Broad College of Business, Department of Supply Chain Management, has an opening for a tenure system assistant professor in Operations Management and Supply Chain Management to start in the 2027-2028 academic year. Duties include research, teaching, and service, and the teaching responsibility would involve Supply Chain or related courses.

Please note that this is a union position represented by the Union of Tenure System Faculty (UTSF). The university is working with the union to establish a collective bargaining agreement.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship, age, disability or protected veteran status.

### **Required Degree**

Doctorate -Supply Chain Management, Operations Management or related field

### **Minimum Requirements**

The position requires a Ph.D. or equivalent degree from an accredited university. Candidates must have a conferred Ph.D. in Supply Chain Management or related field as of the start date of the position, and have a demonstrated record of research excellence, commensurate with their rank.

### **Desired Qualifications**

Preference for candidates whose research focuses on healthcare operations and/or sustainability. Connections to risk and resilience within these supply chains would also be encouraged. Consistent with the language used in our previous search, we would welcome candidates using a range of empirical approaches, including data science, machine learning, and empirical analytics.

### **Required Application Materials**

CV and Cover Letter

Review of applications will begin as early as October 2026, and continue until the position is filled. To ensure full consideration, applications should be received by November 10th, 2026. Applications must be submitted online at: http://careers.msu.edu
  
  
Please reach out to Dr. Shawnee Vickery @ vickery@broad.msu.edu with any questions about the position.

10/10/2026

MSU strives to provide a flexible work environment and this position has been designated as remote-friendly. Remote-friendly means some or all of the duties can be performed remotely as mutually agreed upon.

https://broad.msu.edu/supply-chain-management/

### **Department Statement**

Highly ranked in US News and World Report, the Supply Chain Management Department (https://broad.msu.edu/supply-chain-management/) is the home of internationally recognized faculty who are among the most accomplished scholars and teachers. The department offers a Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, a graduate certificate in Elements of Global Supply Chain Management, an MS in Supply Chain Management, and Ph.Ds in both Logistics Management, and Operations & Sourcing Management. The department contributes heavily to the Executive and Full-time MBA programs, online certificate programs, and is very active in executive education programs.

### **MSU Statement**

Michigan State University has been advancing the common good with uncommon will for more than 160 years. One of the top research universities in the world, MSU pushes the boundaries of discovery and forges enduring partnerships to solve the most pressing global challenges while providing life-changing opportunities to a diverse and inclusive academic community through more than 200 programs of study in 17 degree-granting colleges.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Social Work
jobs.description:
### **Assistant Professor, Social Work**

* 497098

* Full-Time

* Social Work

**Department**: Social Work **Salary**: Commensurate with Experience/Education'

**Description**:

***This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.***

  

The University of Houston-Downtown Social Work Program is seeking candidates for one (1) position at the rank of Tenure-Track Assistant Professor. The successful candidate will teach a 4-3 course load over the two long semesters in a variety of modalities; demonstrate a theory-based and community-engaged teaching philosophy; engage in a research agenda that supports the knowledge base of social work practice; and engage in service to the institution, community, and profession.
  
  
**Required Qualifications**

The individual selected will have:

* Earned a doctoral degree (PhD/DSW) in Social Work or a closely related field, and a MSW from a Council of Social Work Education (CSWE)-accredited social work program
* At least two (2) years of full-time post-MSW practice experience with systems of various sizes
* Experience in teaching or demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching at the college level
* Experience in research and scholarship or demonstrated potential to conduct research and scholarship as part of a clearly articulated and evolving social work research agenda
* Demonstrated commitment to service to the university, community, and/or profession

Preferred Qualifications

* PhD/DSW in Social Work (or be ABD)
* LMSW or LCSW (or is licensure-eligible) issued in the State of Texas
* Experience with face-to-face, hybrid, and online instructional modalities at the undergraduate and/or graduate social work course level
* Ability to teach generalist social work courses at all system levels (micro, mezzo, and macro)
* Experience in developing and implementing service learning and experiential learning activities in curricular and co-curricular settings
* History of publishing peer-reviewed articles and/or publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals of high quality
* Demonstrated experience or commitment to fostering community engagement programs and activities
* Knowledge of and experience working with an array of social service, public health, criminal justice, and/or healthcare agencies in the Greater Houston or other urban areas

To be considered for this position, the candidate must submit:

* A cover letter detailing interest in the tenure-track Assistant Professor faculty position and potential for fit in the UHD Social Work Program
* An updated Curriculum Vitae (please include a list of courses previously taught along with the modality)
* Teaching philosophy statement
* Research/scholarly agenda statement
* Unofficial graduate transcripts showing completion of an MSW degree from a CSWE-accredited program and unofficial transcripts showing completion or progress toward the doctoral degree
* Names and contact information for three professional references (letters will be requested if candidates advance in consideration for the position)

**Review of applications will begin immediately and conclude when the position is filled.**
  
  
The University: Located in the heart of Harris County and the Houston metroplex, the University of Houston-Downtown is a public university that serves the fourth largest city and one of the most diverse student bodies in the nation. UHD offers bachelor's degrees in 44 areas of study and nine master's degrees. Current enrollment is approximately 15,000 students, making UHD the second largest member institution in the University of Houston System. UHD is a federally designated Hispanic and Minority Serving University.
  
  
The College: The College of Public Service (CPS) has two departments: Criminal Justice & Social Work and Urban Education. The college offers four bachelor's degrees and three master's degrees. The college is within walking distance of major police agencies, correctional facilities, and county, state, and federal courts. Additionally, the CPS maintains relationships with key social service providing organizations that serve the Greater Houston area.
  
  
The Department: The Department of Criminal Justice and Social Work offers degree plans leading to the Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice, the Bachelor of Applied Arts and Sciences in Criminal Justice, the Master of Science in Criminal Justice, the Bachelor of Social Work, and Master of Social Work degrees. The department recently added an innovative graduate-level Applied Corrections Certificate that draws on the combined strengths of the criminal justice and the social work faculty of the department.
  
  
The Program: The University of Houston-Downtown’s Social Work Program is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE) and awards a Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) and Master of Social Work (MSW) degree.
  
  
To apply for this position, fill out the online application and submit a Curriculum Vitae, cover letter, teaching philosophy statement, research/scholarly agenda statement, unofficial graduate transcripts, and contact information for three professional references.

The search committee will begin screening applications as early as October 2026, although the system will remain open for applications until the position is filled. Ideally, we will complete the selection process by early Spring 2027.

All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check.

The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

**Essential Job Functions**
The Center for Interdisciplinary Research in Women's Health is currently accepting applications for its NIH-funded K12 faculty training program, “Building
  
  
Interdisciplinary Research Careers in Women’s Health (BIRWCH)” at the Assistant Professor level. This position will become available on August 15, 2027.
  
  
Successful candidates will be expected to devote 75% effort conducting clinical or basic research related to women's health or sex differences, under the
  
  
guidance of two or more senior BIRWCH mentors. At UTMB, the BIRCWH program has five research focus areas: aging, cancer prevention, health
  
  
disparities / Hispanic health, infectious disease, and reproductive health. Each focal area is supported by nationally recognized mentors, chosen for their
  
  
research, mentoring records, and dedication to advancing interdisciplinary women's health research. Successful candidates will also be expected to
  
  
participate in career development activities, as required by the UTMB BIRCWH curriculum (program details available at: https://www.utmb.edu/bircwh).
  
  
Successful candidates are expected to actively participate in intra- and inter-departmental meetings, engage in high-quality research, apply for external
  
  
federal and non-federal funding, publish peer-reviewed manuscripts, and present at regional, national, and international scientific meetings.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Have a PhD degree or clinical doctorate.
* Have completed all postgraduate training including a postdoctoral or clinical fellowship.
* Have no more than 8 years of research experience after their last doctoral degree at program start.

**Preferred Qualifications**
Ideal candidates will have a good publication record, an interest in women's health or sex differences, and demonstrated skills in seeking or obtaining
  
  
research support.
  
  
**Salary**
Commensurate with experience.

jobs.description:
The University of Pittsburgh School of Nursing is seeking qualified applicants for full-time, non-tenure stream, Medical-Surgical faculty in the Department of Acute and Tertiary Care.
  
  
This Appointment-Stream position will be a full-time faculty member in the Acute and Tertiary Care Department in the School of Nursing, who will be responsible for teaching, clinical instruction, scholarship, and service. Responsibilities will include teaching and mentoring students in both the classroom and clinical setting, contributing to course development and delivery, and supporting student learning, professional development, and readiness for practice. Expectations also include active and sustained engagement in scholarship, clinical innovation, and dissemination through publications and presentations. The faculty member will also participate in service activities that support the School, University, profession, and community, contributing to committees, professional organizations, clinical partnerships, and community-based initiatives in alignment with the mission of the institution. Other duties may be assigned based on department needs. Faculty members receive dedicated time and resources to ensure they can successfully conduct their program of research, disseminate their research, and develop professionally. Faculty promotion opportunities are available for all ranks.
  
  
**Faculty Requirements In The Appointment Stream (Non-Tenure Stream)**

* Assistant Professor – A) An earned doctorate in nursing or a field related to the area of scholarship within the School of Nursing is required. B) Evidence of or potential for a sustained and impactful program of scholarship. C) Evidence of or potential for excellence in teaching and mentoring, and contributing to a learning environment that values evidence-based practice.
* Associate Professor – A) An earned doctorate in nursing or a field related to the area of scholarship within the School of Nursing is required. B) Evidence of a sustained and impactful program of scholarship that is nationally recognized. C) Evidence of excellence in teaching and mentoring, and contributing to a learning environment that values evidence-based practice. D) Evidence of or potential for leadership in the field.
* Professor – A) An earned doctorate in nursing or a field related to the area of scholarship within the School of Nursing is required. B) Evidence of a sustained and impactful program of scholarship that is internationally recognized. C) Evidence of excellence in teaching and mentoring, and contributing to a learning environment that values evidence-based practice. D) Evidence of leadership in the field.

**About The University Of Pittsburgh School Of Nursing**
Since its founding in 1939, the University of Pittsburgh School of Nursing has provided faculty and students with the resources and support to generate new healthcare knowledge and the educational foundation to conduct evidence-based practice, engage in scholarly activities, and translate knowledge to improve the delivery of healthcare in Pennsylvania, the nation, and throughout the world.
  
  
As one of the nation's elite schools of nursing, Pitt Nursing receives millions of dollars in NIH grant funding each year, and U.S. News & World Report highly ranks multiple academic programs. **Apply Now**
Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. Candidates should apply online at https://www.join.pitt.edu/ and search for requisition number: 26006228. For more information on the School of Nursing, visit www.nursing.pitt.edu.
  
  
As part of your application, please provide a statement of your area of scholarship and why you believe you will be successful at Pitt Nursing.

jobs.description:
The Department of History at Thiel College invites applications for a tenure-track position in United States History. Teaching responsibilities will include American surveys and upper-division courses in United States History. Areas of specialization are open, but preference will be given to candidates whose teaching and professional interests support the preparation of future history educators and the use of technology to enhance history instruction, historical research, and student learning.

Candidates should have an interest in joining an undergraduate department where teaching in a small classroom environment is emphasized. Expectations include a 4/4 teaching load, developing engaging pedagogy, openness to interdisciplinary courses, advising, and active involvement in the campus community. Candidates must have a Doctorate in History; candidates currently completing doctoral work will also be considered.

A dedicated passion for helping students reach their full potential in a supportive and inclusive, diverse environment is essential to this position. Responsibilities include teaching, advising, student supervision, and professional development. While Thiel College gives highest priority to teaching effectiveness, faculty are expected to remain current in the field through professional development opportunities such as attendance at related conferences, research, or other scholarly activities. A comprehensive employee benefit package, including research support and a sabbatical program, is provided.

Thiel College welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Please note, however, that we are unable to provide employment visa sponsorship (e.g., H-1B) for this position. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

**To Apply:**

Thiel College welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Please note, however, that we are unable to provide employment visa sponsorship (e.g., H-1B) for this position. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

Applicants should:

* Submit a letter of interest, curriculum vitae and list of references (all these materials should be attached in a single PDF document using candidate’s name as the document title) by clicking here.
* Additional required materials, including transcripts, sample syllabi for both a survey and an upper-division U.S. history course, and summaries of recent teaching evaluations, if available, should be sent in PDF format to employment@thiel.edu (preferred option). These items may also be mailed to Jennifer Clark, Director of Human Resources, Thiel College, 75 College Avenue, Greenville, PA. 16125.

Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

Thiel College is committed to attracting culturally and professionally diverse faculty and staff who engage our students by providing a rich and fulfilling curricular and co-curricular experience.

**About Thiel College**

Thiel College is an independent liberal arts college rooted in the Lutheran tradition. Thiel College empowers individuals to reach their full potential by creating a diverse and inclusive learning environment that ensures educational excellence, stimulates global awareness, and promotes ethical leadership. In doing so, Thiel prepares students for careers and lives of meaning and purpose.

**About the Area**

Greenville is in northwestern Pennsylvania, a 90-minute drive from both Pittsburgh and Cleveland and a 40-minute drive from Youngstown, Ohio. Greenville and the surrounding areas have scenic parks, trails, and waterways for relaxing, hiking, camping, and boating. The area has a low cost of living, making it a desirable location for young professionals and growing families.

jobs.title: Practice Professor of Nursing-Sexual Reproductive Health & Nurse Midwifery
jobs.description:
The
**University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing**
, one of 12 Schools in a highly ranked institution, is dedicated to the integration of interdisciplinary research, education, and practice.
  
  
The Family and Community Health (FCH) Department in the School of Nursing seeks candidates for an associated faculty position on the non-tenure practice track. We invite individuals prepared at the doctoral level (PhD or DNP) to apply to the Associated faculty (Practice Track at rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor).
  
  
Applicants must have content expertise in sexual reproductive health, women’s health, and/or nurse-midwifery. Teaching responsibilities may include courses in the Women’s Health Gender Related (WHGRNP) Nurse Practitioner program, Nurse-Midwifery program, and our BSN and MPN programs.
  
  
The Women’s Health/Gender-Related Nurse Practitioner program focuses on the primary, sexual, and reproductive health care needs of women from adolescence through the advanced years, concentrating on promoting and maintaining wellness. The Nurse-Midwifery program prepares graduates for midwifery practice focused on providing family-centered, comprehensive care for fundamentally healthy people and their families. The BSN and MPN programs both include courses focused on sexual reproductive health and nursing of women and infants.
  
  
The Practice Professor may have teaching responsibilities in both the entry-to-practice (BSN & MPN) and graduate programs. Experience in academic program leadership, curriculum development/evaluation, academic teaching using multiple modalities (didactic, online) and working with an interprofessional audience of physicians and nurses is preferred. Strong analytical skills with the ability to assimilate numerous sources of complex information is required. Excellent writing skills are essential. Strong interpersonal and organizational skills needed.
  
  
The candidate must be licensed as a Registered Nurse (RN) in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania or be eligible for licensure, with acquisition of the RN license within the first semester of employment. For those who will teach in the Women’s Health/Gender-Related Nurse Practitioner (WHGRNP) Program, the candidate must also be licensed as a Certified Registered Nurse Practitioner (CRNP) in Pennsylvania or be eligible for licensure, with acquisition of the CRNP license within the first semester of employment. Current national board certification is required. For those who will teach in the Nurse-Midwifery Program, the candidate must be licensed as a Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM) in Pennsylvania or be eligible for licensure, with acquisition of the CNM license within the first semester of employment. Current certification by the American Midwifery Certification Board (AMCB) is required.
  
  
**Qualifications:**
Academic teaching experience is required and should meet minimum qualifications for the Practice Professor track:
  
  

* Achieves consistently high-level quality teaching via peer review and student evaluations.
* Identifies and applies creative teaching and evaluation methods within the curricular framework identified by the SON.
* Demonstrates leadership in curriculum development.
* Demonstrates excellence in depth and breadth of knowledge in the content being taught.
* Contributes in significant ways to the design, implementation, and evaluation of programmatic educational offerings within the SON.
* Demonstrates impact in his/her area of expertise through a consistent record of publications, consultations, presentations, and panels at local and regional forums.
* Demonstrates excellence in student advising and mentoring.
* Mentors faculty in other tracks (e.g. lecturer positions) and/or mentors teaching assistants

Interested Applicants please submit Cover Letter and CV

**Summary**
-----------

The School of Inclusive Teacher Education invites applications for a tenure track Assistant/Associate Professor in Reading to start August 2027. Applicants should have experience with evidence-based literacy instruction and expertise in areas such as reading disabilities and dyslexia, assessment, intervention, and professional development. In addition to teaching and service responsibilities, this position will also support BGSU’s Structured Literacy Center through research activities including publication and grant-writing. This is a nine-month appointment with the option to teach in the summer for extra compensation.
  
  
**Information about Program and College**
  
The School of Inclusive Teacher Education supports the University’s initial teacher licensure programs which
  
span grades PreK-12 and graduate programs in Special Education, Reading, and Curriculum and Teaching. The Graduate Reading programs lead to an Ohio K-12 reading endorsement and a Master of Education degree.
  
  
The mission of the School of Inclusive Teacher Education is to build and sustain a dynamic, collaborative
  
community of highly skilled teachers for all levels of education, thereby increasing graduates’ options and
  
those of their students for lives as independent, productive, and contributing citizens. The School is committed to rigorous scholarship, innovative teaching and learning, and civic and professional engagement that places high value on the diversity of individuals and communities in a global society. There are approximately 2000 undergraduate students and more than 500 graduate students in seven initial licensure programs and four graduate programs, with numerous endorsements and certificates. These programs are guided by nearly fifty full-time faculty and staff.
  
  
The College of Education and Human Development, BGSU's founding college, is the home to a dynamic and disciplinary diverse group of graduate and undergraduate programs, housed across three academic units: the School of Applied Human Development; the School of Counseling, Higher Education, Leadership, and Foundations; and the School of Inclusive Teacher Education. The College is committed to promoting and supporting a community of inclusion, collaboration, and respect for students, faculty, and staff. A strong sense of community serves as the central tenet for the College’s priorities for integrating professional preparation, leadership and service, experiential learning, and inquiry and innovation in all academic programs and related experiences. The College has extensive partnerships across professional, school, and community settings that facilitate collaboration for student experiences and research opportunities.
  
  
*As a Public University for the Public Good*, **Bowling Green State University** is a comprehensive, high research university located in northwestern Ohio committed to driving economic and cultural vitality in the region and beyond. Through innovative teaching, research and creative activities, BGSU fosters a collaborative and inclusive learning community where inspired ideas, knowledge and achievements support the region, state and nation. More than 760 talented and passionate faculty members teach across more than 200 undergraduate majors and programs, 17 doctoral programs, and 57 master’s programs. A focus on promoting research, scholarship, and creative activities has resulted in a significant increase in extramural funding over the past several years.
  
  
Guided by Forward, BGSU’s strategic plan, the University is focused on redefining student success. For the fifth year in a row, The Wall Street Journal ranks BGSU as the No. 1 public university in the Midwest that students would choose again. BGSU also holds the Wall Street Journal distinction of being the No. 1 public university in Ohio for the student experience.

**Essential Functions**
-----------------------

1. Teach up to three courses per semester in the Graduate Reading Programs. Courses may include:
  
Diverse Reader Profiles/MTSS, Phonics Intervention, Comprehension/Vocabulary Intervention, Writing
  
Intervention, Seminar in Literacy Research, and Literacy Coaching. Courses may be taught in-person or
  
online (asynchronous) and may include evenings.
  
2. Maintain a strong research agenda in support of BGSU’s Structured Literacy Center that leads to
  
successful publication, external presentations, community engagement, and ongoing external funding
  
for the Center.
  
3. Collaborate in Structured Literacy Center and program development and participate in student
  
advising.
  
4. Contribute and provide leadership to the school, college, university, and the profession through service
  
activities.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

1. Earned doctorate in Reading or Literacy, Early Childhood Education, Elementary Education, Curriculum
  
and Instruction, or a closely related field with a focus on reading or literacy.
  
2. Demonstrated evidence of scholarly effectiveness, including research investigations, publications,
  
presentations at professional conferences, and/or grant writing.
  
3. A minimum of two years professional experience teaching reading (e.g., classroom teacher,
  
special education teacher, reading specialist, or other related service provider in educational
  
settings) or equivalent.
  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**
  
1. Attained tenure and promotion to the Associate professor rank at a comparable institution.
  
2. Certification (or the ability to obtain certification) in Structured Literacy approach or Ohio Department
  
of Education and Workforce approved program.
  
3. Experience teaching at the college level in multiple modalities (e.g., in-person, online).
  
4. Experience obtaining external funding and/or managing externally funded projects.
  
5. Experience leading a team, program, or group research project.

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

Application Materials Required
  

* Cover letter
* Curriculum vitae
* Names and contact information of three professional references

  
Unofficial transcripts of highest degree earned are required for candidates invited for in-person interviews.
  
  
Finalist will be required to submit official transcripts.
  
  
BGSU policy requires finalist to authorize and pass a background check prior to receiving an offer of
  
employment.
  
  
Application Deadline
  
The search committee will review applications until the position is filled; however, for best consideration,
  
applications should be provided by **November 1, 2026.**
  
  
Salary & Benefits
  
Competitive and commensurate with candidate’s experience and credentials. Full benefits package available.
  
  
Further Information
  
Contact Dr. Tracy Huziak-Clark, School Director, School of Inclusive Teacher Education at: thuziak@bgsu.edu.

jobs.description:
**Business Faculty**
====================

Northwestern College invites applications for a full-time business faculty position beginning in August 2027. The teaching load is 24 credit hours per academic year. In addition to classroom instruction, the successful candidate will engage in scholarly activity and institutional service, including advising students, supervising program activities, and recruiting for the business and economics programs.

We are seeking a versatile educator who can seamlessly bridge specialized agricultural courses with high-demand business offerings. Roughly half of the teaching load will focus on the agricultural business curriculum—delivering foundational and advanced courses such as Introduction to Ag Business, Ag Technology Systems, Ag Issues and Ethics, and Ag Risk and Cost Management, alongside overseeing student internships, practicums and advising the student Ag Club. The remaining portion of the load will support our core business program by teaching essential courses like Business Writing, Principles of Marketing, Consumer Behavior, Integrated Marketing Communication, and Small Business Management, with opportunities to introduce electives aligned with your specific scholarly or professional expertise.

**Required Qualifications:** Applicants must hold at least a master’s degree in agricultural business, agricultural education, business administration or a closely related field, with candidates holding a master’s degree and significant professional experience considered for an instructor or professor of practice role. We seek faculty members who are committed to excellence in teaching, active scholarly engagement and the mission of the liberal arts as a vital expression of Christ's redemptive work in the world.

**Preferred Qualifications:** Preference will be given to candidates holding an earned Ph.D. or terminal degree in agricultural business, business administration or a closely related field for a tenure-track appointment (ABD candidates considered). Ideal candidates will demonstrate excellence in undergraduate teaching, maintain research that engages students and show a strong commitment to relationship-centered mentorship. We seek a collaborative colleague who will enrich our departmental culture through service, shared purpose and a dedication to helping students flourish academically, professionally and personally.

*Northwestern College seeks candidates with an authentic Christian faith who will embrace and live out our* *mission & values**, including our Reformed, evangelical and ecumenical identity as stated in our Christian Identity Statement, Mission Statement, Vision for Learning and Vision for Diversity.
